```{r}
#install.packages(c("tidyverse", "caret", "glmnet", "MASS", "car", "class"))
#install.packages("LaTeX")
```
```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(glmnet)
library(MASS)
library(car)
```

```{r}
df <- read.csv("final_data_with_changes.csv")

head(df)
str(df)
summary(df)
names(df)
```

```{r}
colSums(is.na(df))

df <- na.omit(df)
```

```{r}
df$log_price <- log(df$price)
```

The response variable (price) exhibited strong right-skewness. A logarithmic transformation was applied to normalize the distribution, stabilize variance, and improve the performance and interpretability of regression models.

```{r}
#converting categorical variables
df <- df %>%
  mutate_if(is.character, as.factor)
```

All character variables were converted into factors to ensure proper handling of categorical predictors. This enables the regression model to internally generate dummy variables and incorporate qualitative features effectively.

```{r}
set.seed(123)

trainIndex <- createDataPartition(df$log_price, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)

train <- df[trainIndex, ]
test  <- df[-trainIndex, ]

```

The dataset was divided into training (70%) and testing (30%) subsets using stratified sampling. The training set was used to build predictive models, while the test set was used to evaluate model performance on unseen data.

```{r}
train_clean <- train %>% dplyr::select(-price_total)
test_clean  <- test  %>% dplyr::select(-price_total)
```

#### PHASE 3: MULTIPLE LINEAR REGRESSION
##### Y = $beta$0 + ...
###### fit model
```{r}
lm_model <- lm(log_price ~ ., data = train)

pred_lm <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test)
```

```{r}
rmse <- function(actual, predicted) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
}

mae <- function(actual, predicted) {
  mean(abs(actual - predicted))
}

cat("Linear Regression:\n")
cat("RMSE:", rmse(test$log_price, pred_lm), "\n")
cat("MAE:", mae(test$log_price, pred_lm), "\n")
```
#### Residual Plot
```{r}
plot(lm_model$fitted.values, lm_model$residuals)
abline(h = 0, col = "red")
```
#### Cook’s Distance
```{r}
cooksd <- cooks.distance(lm_model)
plot(cooksd, type="h")
```
#### Stepwise Selection
```{r}
step_model <- stepAIC(lm_model, direction = "both")

summary(step_model)
```
```{r}
#model comparison
AIC(lm_model, step_model)
BIC(lm_model, step_model)
```
### Regularisation
```{r}
x_train <- model.matrix(log_price ~ . - price_total, train)[,-1]

y_train <- train$log_price

x_test <- model.matrix(log_price ~ . - price_total, test)[,-1]
y_test <- test$log_price

```

#Ridge Regression
```{r}
ridge_model <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 0)

ridge_pred <- predict(ridge_model, s = "lambda.min", newx = x_test)

cat("Ridge RMSE:", rmse(y_test, ridge_pred), "\n")
```
#Lasso
```{r}
lasso_model <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 1)

lasso_pred <- predict(lasso_model, s = "lambda.min", newx = x_test)

cat("LASSO RMSE:", rmse(y_test, lasso_pred), "\n")
```
#Elastic Net
```{r}
elastic_model <- cv.glmnet(x_train, y_train, alpha = 0.5)

elastic_pred <- predict(elastic_model, s = "lambda.min", newx = x_test)

cat("Elastic Net RMSE:", rmse(y_test, elastic_pred), "\n")
```
### PHASE 7: KNN REGRESSION
#Normalize Data
```{r}
preProc <- preProcess(train[, -c(which(names(train) %in% c("price","log_price")))], method = c("center", "scale"))

train_scaled <- predict(preProc, train)
test_scaled  <- predict(preProc, test)
```
#Apply KNN
```{r}
knn_model <- knnreg(log_price ~ . - price_total, data = train_scaled, k = 5)

knn_pred <- predict(knn_model, newdata = test_scaled)

cat("KNN RMSE:", rmse(test$log_price, knn_pred), "\n")
```
### PHASE 8: GLM (UNIT 5)
```{r}
#Fit GLM
glm_model <- glm(log_price ~ . - price_total, data = train, family = gaussian(link = "identity"))

summary(glm_model)
```
#Model Comparison
```{r}
results <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Linear", "Stepwise", "Ridge", "LASSO", "Elastic", "KNN"),
  RMSE = c(
    rmse(test$log_price, pred_lm),
    rmse(test$log_price, predict(step_model, test)),
    rmse(y_test, ridge_pred),
    rmse(y_test, lasso_pred),
    rmse(y_test, elastic_pred),
    rmse(test$log_price, knn_pred)
  )
)

print(results[order(results$RMSE), ])
```
```{r}
#final model

best_model <- step_model  # or whichever has lowest RMSE

final_pred <- predict(best_model, newdata = test)
```
